brief.subtitle: A working document for our November 11 call
letter: I've been thinking a lot about what we talked about on our call, and I wanted to get all of it down on paper before we meet again.

This is my first draft of what a SkyyTask × ShootPortal partnership could look like: the idea, how the two platforms would work together, what your pilots and clients would see, roughly what it would cost, and the steps to get there.
Nothing here is set in stone. Please mark it up. Tell me what you like, what you don't, and what I'm missing, so we can spend our time on the 11th on what matters most to you.
brief.oneLiner: SkyyTask keeps the job, the chat and the client. ShootPortal quietly takes over the files: a branded upload for the pilot, a beautiful delivery page for the client, and an automatic update back to SkyyTask at every step.
questions: When should a job appear in ShootPortal: when it's accepted, or when the pilot taps Complete Job?
Should clients get a branded email from us, a link in your SkyyTask chat, or both?
Do you still want a one-time code, or is a private link enough?
What should release a pilot's pay: submitted, viewed, or downloaded?
Roughly how many jobs a month, and how big are typical deliveries?
Does the pricing feel fair and easy to plan around?
Which enterprise file types matter most (thermal, mapping, point clouds, reports)?
What's missing, or what would you do differently?
